newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: UN body urges economic balance in Asia-Pacific.
newsitem.headline: UN body urges economic balance in Asia-Pacific.

text.p: Developing countries of the Asia-Pacific must balance the negative impacts of liberalisation and deregulation against international obligations, a United Nations body said in an annual survey released on Wednesday.

The survey by the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) said developing countries may no longer rely on traditional measures such as subsidies, directed credit and tariff and non-tariff barriers to diversify exports.
"The obligations of the Uruguay Round impose a degree of constraint on the application of some of these measures," the survey said.
ESCAP urged developing countries to review the world trade agreement and design policies accordingly.
Developing countries should put "safety nets" in place to address the unemployment and labour displacement that will likely result from reforms, the survey said.

On foreign direct investment, the survey said developing countries should adopt policies that encourage reinvestment of profits and investment in export-oriented sectors in order to avoid balance of payments pressures.
Regional cooperation initiatives should attempt to achieve a reasonable degree of equity in the distribution of gains among participating countries, the survey said.
The survey also said the international community should improve the environment for developing countries to participate in economic globalisation.
A big help, ESCAP said, would be to ensure full implementation of the world trade agreement and market access for exports of lesser-developed countries.
ESCAP is part of the United Nations Development Programme.
